tools.description: Discover accessible product libraries for DIY, wardrobe, cabinet, and door/window domains. Returns opaque references required by all library-scoped tools. Discovery does not open or change the product panel. For custom-domain public libraries, query descending numeric priority first; inspect candidates from higher-priority libraries before expanding to lower-priority libraries. Equal-priority libraries retain their returned order. Image search is domain-wide and cannot enforce library priority.

Run one to five ordered text queries against a discovered account library. This covers custom-domain public libraries and enterprise libraries. Omit nodeRef and folderRef to search the library's complete discovered root scope. Results with usable=false or available=false are pagination placeholders only. Never select them for placement, replacement, or any product-use operation. For custom-domain public libraries, query descending numeric priority first; inspect candidates from higher-priority libraries before expanding to lower-priority libraries. Equal-priority libraries retain their returned order. Image search is domain-wide and cannot enforce library priority. For product selection, explicitly use limit=8, includeImages=true and imageLimit=8. Inspect every returned preview, match it to its product reference, and compare actual appearance to the user intent or reference image. Do not choose solely by product name, result rank, or a returned refinement. Treat missing or failed images as unverified, never as visually reviewed. With a reference image use both text search and image search and select from their combined visual results. If no candidate is suitable and page.hasMore is true, continue using page.nextOffset with the same keyword and constraints; inspect all previews on the next page. Report exhausted or unavailable results honestly instead of forcing a selection. Read returned dimensions when comparing size constraints: searchData.size.x/y/z represent current/default W (width), D (depth), H (height). For adjustable custom products, searchData.width/depth/height describe dimensions and units, and searchData.parameters W/D/H may provide value, min/max or discrete options. Distinguish a current value from a continuous range and discrete choices. Use returned length units; chargeUnit is a pricing unit, not a length unit. Do not fill missing dimensions with zero or treat a combination bounding size as a component size.

Prefer precise category plus a reliable primary feature, not a long visual sentence or invented search syntax. Do not treat a removable seat cushion as the chair frame material. An empty string browses by category or filters.

tools.description: Search the selected domain-wide public product scope with an HTTP(S) image or raw Base64 file bytes. File input is validated and uploaded through the existing product-image service. The tool cannot restrict image search to an enterprise library. Before calling, inspect the entire source image with the proposed bounding box overlaid; an automatically detected box is only a draft. Manually correct it when necessary. Select the entire visible target: include all visible table top and legs, or chair back, frame, seat and legs; do not crop just a material patch or cushion. Do not invent occluded or off-image parts. This tool has no pagination parameter; if unsuitable, refine the bounding box or continue paged text search. Results with usable=false or available=false are pagination placeholders only. Never select them for placement, replacement, or any product-use operation. For product selection, explicitly use limit=8, includeImages=true and imageLimit=8. Inspect every returned preview, match it to its product reference, and compare actual appearance to the user intent or reference image. Do not choose solely by product name, result rank, or a returned refinement. Treat missing or failed images as unverified, never as visually reviewed. With a reference image use both text search and image search and select from their combined visual results. Distinguish a current value from a continuous range and discrete choices. Use returned length units; chargeUnit is a pricing unit, not a length unit.
